Spot premium quotations for imported cathode rallied over the past two weeks. Traders reported that the latest spot premium quotations for imported cathode were in the US$110-140/t range, whereas spot premium quotations for SXEW were quoted between US$100-110/t. The SHFE/LME cash month price ratio continues to benefit cathode imports. Traders and cathode importers for financing have shown more interest in the import business. However, some market insiders believe that commercial banks have placed restrictions on issuing letters of credit for the import of cathode as collateral involved in the re- © 2011 CRU International Limited **confidential** **September 2011** www.crumonitor.com export business, especially in Zhejiang province. This comes after China’s central bank announced that it will expand the scope of deposits involved with the reserve requirement. Therefore, recently there has been slightly more cathode inflow than outflow from Shanghai bonded warehouses. We estimate that copper cathode housed in these stocks currently amounts to around 300,000t. According to Chinese customs data, China imported 235,509t of cathode in August, up 21.2% m-o-m but still down 11.9% y-o-y. The figure is higher than market expectations but is still considered reasonable. We understand that the major reason for the import rally is a more favourable arbitrage, spurred on from increased spot buying. We expect that cathode imports will continue to rise month-on-month in September as the SHFE/LME arbitrage persists or widens, boosting import figures. # **China’s Q4 copper consumption outlook** Copper prices slumped from early August, dampened by the financial market turmoil. Previously, during the copper price retreat in May we saw the Shanghai physical market move to trade at a premium i.e. the Shanghai physical copper price was higher than the SHFE cash month price. However, this time China’s physical demand did not act as a copper price support when prices dropped. We understand that China’s copper consumption outlook in Q4 is very important to the copper market from a fundamentals point-ofview. Will it slow down the price slump or even drive a price rally together with the tight concentrate and scrap supply? Until now it seems China’s copper consumption outlook in Q4 is not optimistic. We were

told by copper wirerod producers that against tightened credit the high financial cost and low profit margins continue to challenge businesses, especially those in the privately-owned enterprise sector.  Some wirerod producers anticipate wirerod demand in Q4 may be weaker than in Q3 if domestic credit remains tightened.  Copper plate strip and sheet (PSS) producers have said that the outlook for new orders is not good.  Copper PSS usage in autos and electrical industry has declined.  Whereas, copper tube producers expect demand may recover in October as the traditionally stronger season approaches.  As we mentioned in the last fortnightly, copper tube consumption declined in August and September. Some semis producers reflect that they are undecided as to whether they will purchase more copper when copper price declined below RMB60,000/t.  We believe that the price slump and lack of immediate recovery is not only as a result of negative market sentiment due to the financial news but also due to constrained buying ability. 

# **Home appliance to rural area stimulus ends** 

According to a joint notice issued by the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Commerce and Industry and the Information Technology Ministry, the home appliance to rural area policy will end in the first trial provinces and cities including Shandong, Qingdao, Henan and Sichuan on 30<sup>th</sup> November 2011.  The stimulus will end in the other 14 provinces and cities including Inner Mongolia, Liaoning, Dalian, Heilongjiang, Anhui, Hubei, Hunan, Guangxi, Chongqing and Shaanxi by the end of November 2012. The policy will end in the rest of the country by the end of January 2013.  Based on data from the Ministry of Commerce, cumulative sales of home appliances to the countryside until the end of August this year was 180 million units, achieving a sales revenue of RMB405 billion. While the market understands the negative impact from the stimulus withdrawal is inevitable in the short term, home appliance sales have already declined since April 2011 along with the policy’s stimulating effect.  At the same time, some local governments are in arrears with financial subsidies.  Moreover, home appliance to rural area tender are released every October and the product price is fixed by the end of the year, but raw material prices have continued to rise since H2 2010, negatively affecting white goods producers profits.  All the factors mentioned above will offset the negative impact of stimulus withdrawal to some extent. We believe that as rural residents incomes increase and home appliances are replaced, demand for home appliances in rural areas will grow in the future.

The LME 3-month copper price plummeted to around $7,400/t as confidence in the financial markets collapsed. It seems $8,000/t is not an effective support for the copper market and prices continued to fall in the LME market to around $7,200/t. The Federal Reserve did not roll out a QE3 and stressed the significant downside risk for U.S. economy. After that China and European PMI data further dampened market sentiment. Similarly, the SHFE 3-month copper price hit a low on 23th September, closing at RMB56,940/t, down 14.7% compared to two weeks ago. We noticed that the Shanghai physical market premium widened as the SHFE cash month copper prices slumped. The latest average premium is RMB400/t. However, it is too early to say physical demand can support the copper price. The copper market is currently falling through panic selling. Most consumers are concerned about prices falling further and will therefore wait for price to stabilise before re-entering the market. Very few consumers are choosing to buy low as they are preparing for scaled-down operations in the first week of October which is a national holiday. According to the latest data, SHFE cathode inventories declined to 102,253t, down 11,047t compared to two weeks ago. © 2011 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 4 **September 2011** www.crumonitor.com We believe that in the context of the Eurozone debt crisis and concern about the global economic outlook, the copper market will still be dominated by negative macro news in the short term. A possibility exists that the copper price may rally after dropping significantly. However, the copper market will maintain its bearish sentiment. We anticipate that the SHFE 3 month copper price will test RMB53,000-55000/t support. The copper price will see more volatility when the SHFE closes and the LME remains open for trading during China’s national holidays. ## **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **Grace Qu (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2206, ext. 321 grace.qu@crugroup.com **James Wright (London):** +44 20 7903 2052 james.wright@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 23rd September, 2011.
